sources.entry: Marker Data - The avant-garde Marker extraction application crafted for Final Cut Pro. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/TheAcharya/MarkerData)

summary.one_liner: Marker Data is a macOS app that extracts Final Cut Pro markers and converts them into formats such as CSV, Excel, Notion or Airtable databases, YouTube chapters, MIDI, and PDFs.
summary.what_it_does: The app reads Final Cut Pro marker metadata and exports it through a set of extract profiles, including Notion (JSON), Airtable (JSON), CSV, TSV, XLSX, YouTube Chapters, Compressor Chapters, Markdown, SubRip subtitles, and Standard MIDI File. It can batch extract and render stills or animated GIFs at each marker's timecode, and can analyse images to embed colour swatches. It can also burn labels and marker metadata onto stills or GIFs, and create PDFs via Pagemaker. The README says it integrates with Final Cut Pro as a Share Destination and Workflow Extension, supports Projects and Compound Clips, and can sync markers to cloud databases with one click. It uses the MarkersExtractor library, with a CLI and library maintained separately.
use_cases: Export Final Cut Pro markers to a spreadsheet
Send markers to Notion or Airtable databases
Create YouTube chapters from a timeline
Build a shot library with stills and colour swatches
Send markers to audio DAWs as MIDI
how_to_run: Download the DMG from the project's release page.
Mount the DMG by double-clicking it.
Move Marker Data to your Applications folder.
Read the onboarding information and instructions.
notable: Native Final Cut Pro Share Destination and Workflow Extension
Exports to many formats, including Notion and Airtable JSON and Standard MIDI File
Batch still and animated GIF rendering at marker timecodes
Automatic colour swatch analysis embedded in extracted images
caveats: Requires macOS Sequoia 15.7 or later and Apple silicon Macs only
Requires Final Cut Pro 12.0 or later (Lifetime or Creator Studio subscription)
Must be installed in the Applications folder to work correctly
An internet connection is needed for some modules and functionality
